column1: # How each monitor capture becomes gate rows (`prove`, docs/MONITOR.md): metadata only (source ids, capture keys,
# gate files, entries, members, points), never a printed time. One line a row to add per capture whose days the gate
# does not hold yet at that row's entry, member and point; every row is split=test (held out).
# What a row reads is never written here: its columns, zone, format, school and clock come from its family, the latest
# row of the same gate file, entry, member and point that reads an earlier capture of the same source and key; else
# such a row whose table prints the same as the capture on every day both hold; else the fetcher's own metadata in the
# monitor's index. A convention changed in a gate file is therefore inherited by the next capture.
# - capture: the index keys (`*` any run of characters).
# - entry: `index` (the capture's own entry as the index names it, read at its unit's point when it names one, else at
#   its own), `same` (every row of the gate file that reads an earlier capture of this source and key, cloned: its
#   entry, member and point; with member * and point same), or an entry (`id` or `id/unit`).
# - member: `-`, `index` (the index's entry is the member: a cautious entry's member row), or a member id.
# - point: `index`, `unit` (the unit's own point), `all` (every point the gate file reads this entry and member at),
# - days: `all`; `month` (the month the capture's key ends with, yyyy-mm: a cautious entry's members for the month a
#   member published); `excused` (without the days the gate file's @excuse lines excuse for the member, ruling R117).
# - from: `-` (the capture itself) or another capture, `<source>/<key>` with {yyyy} and {mm} from this capture's key.
# A line whose capture is the bare `*` does not apply to a capture another line of the same source and gate file names
# more specifically: Kemenag's fetcher names the five kota of the round of 29 September 2026 by their point alone, and
# the gate holds them as units, so each is given its unit on a line of its own.
# A source's own entry is read at a named point, never `all`: Amman's region table at Amman's point alone (ruling R30,
# a table checked for the place it is printed for), however many other points jo.awqaf is read at; `all` is for the
# cautious members, whose table is the member's for every point of the entry.
# Not here: the hand-read sources (manual in sources.tsv), the Mawaqit surveys (calendars, checked by their surveys),
# and members no fetcher reads (Cape Town's community calendar, masjids.co.za's relay: read by hand each month).
# London Unified: one table for the whole M25 (ruling R44), so a new year is read at every point the gate file reads LUPT at, the unit's own and the twelve edges, as the 2026 rows are.
# The reach rows (sa-ummalqura-reach.tsv, kz-qmdb-reach.tsv; generateReachRows): each measured unit's own table
# replayed across its reach, a line per unit, so that each new year of a unit's table is read at every point of
# its reach too (`all`: the points the reach file reads that unit at). The pattern ends `-2*` so that a place's
# key never names another's (riyadh-2027, not riyadh-al-khabra-2027).
